product_description: Small-batch, bolt-on-neck electric guitar using a CNC-cut structural core or chambered chassis with bonded hardboard/HDF face and back skins, opaque low-cycle finish, modular electronics, and standardized hardware.

body_architecture.core_role: structural chassis carrying neck pocket, bridge anchorage, and cavity walls
body_architecture.skin_role: bonded face and back surfaces providing finish substrate and closing chambers
body_architecture.bonding_process: vacuum-bag lamination with a single cure cycle bonding both skins
body_architecture.indexing_method: index pins registering core and both skins before adhesive open time expires

materials.core_family: sheet or dimensional utility hardwood (governed estimate input, not a product invariant)

provenance.note: Neutral reference architecture for internal manufacturing-cost modeling. Not a branded model.

notes: INTERNAL product definition for manufacturing-estimate development only.
Not a customer catalog item and not a representation of any protected brand or model.
Contains no cost, price, or margin fields by design.

materials.core_family is intentionally a family, not a species. Variant A (plywood core) and Variant B (poplar core) are governed ESTIMATE INPUTS against this one product identity, so cost per saleable unit can be compared without forking the product.

construction.neck_sourcing is 'shop_machined': the neck is CNC-machined in house from blank and fretboard stock, not purchased complete. This materially shifts cost from purchased components into direct build labor and adds independent fretwork yield risk.

body_architecture.chambered is true, but chamber geometry is not yet dimensioned. Chamber volume affects both machining time and final body weight, and is a required input to THIN-SKIN-PILOT-CAPTURE-1.

No acoustic or structural validation has been performed on this architecture. Bond-line durability under string tension, neck-pocket bearing strength in a laminated core, and skin telegraphing over chambers are open engineering questions, not settled assumptions.
